identity.real_world_identity_notes: The observed AC EVO name maps to Alfa Romeo's 1965 Giulia Sprint 1600 GTA, the lightweight 1570 cc GTA based on the Giulia Sprint GT and developed as a road-legal basis for touring-car competition. The FIA Historic Database lists the Giulia Sprint GTA under homologation number 1395 with a 1570 cc engine and an August 2, 1965 homologation date. This is the early 1600 GTA, not the later GTA 1300 Junior, 1750/2000 GTAm, standard Giulia Sprint GT, or the modern Giulia GTA/GTAm.

The official Alfa Romeo museum identifies the Giulia Sprint GTA and its 1570 cc, five-speed, dry single-disc clutch specification. Stellantis identifies the production model as the Giulia Sprint 1600 GTA, presented in 1965 and used as a touring-car basis. FIA records independently establish the exact Giulia Sprint GTA homologation identity and date.

claims.basis: The official Alfa Romeo museum identifies the Giulia Sprint GTA and its 1570 cc, five-speed, dry single-disc clutch specification. Stellantis identifies the production model as the Giulia Sprint 1600 GTA, presented in 1965 and used as a touring-car basis. FIA records independently establish the exact Giulia Sprint GTA homologation identity and date.

The official Alfa Romeo museum lists five forward gears plus reverse, and an exact-model specification corroborates five forward speeds. The exact-model specification identifies the five-speed gearbox as fully synchronized; the official museum independently identifies the five-speed GTA transmission. The period driving impression directly calls the GTA selector a dogleg shifter. Dogleg is a manual H-gate form, while the official museum establishes the physical five-speed manual/clutch configuration. The reviewed sources did not establish the remaining technique and wheel fields, which stay unknown in the real-car baseline: /authentic_controls/steering/wheel_rim/integrated_display, /authentic_controls/steering/wheel_rim/open_top, /authentic_controls/steering/wheel_rim/shape, /authentic_controls/steering/wheel_rim/shift_lights, /authentic_controls/transmission/downshift/automatic_blip, /authentic_controls/transmission/downshift/automatic_cut, /authentic_controls/transmission/downshift/clutch, /authentic_controls/transmission/downshift/manual_blip, /authentic_controls/transmission/downshift/throttle_lift, /authentic_controls/transmission/shift_pattern, /authentic_controls/transmission/standing_start_clutch, /authentic_controls/transmission/upshift/automatic_blip, /authentic_controls/transmission/upshift/automatic_cut, /authentic_controls/transmission/upshift/clutch, /authentic_controls/transmission/upshift/manual_blip, /authentic_controls/transmission/upshift/throttle_lift.
Directly observed during the guided drive: move-off, shift clutch use, automatic cut and blip, and the cockpit rim.

The reviewed sources establish a fully synchronised five-speed gearbox. Synchronisers match the shaft speeds themselves, so the blip eases them rather than engaging the gear, and the value follows from the construction this record already establishes. AC EVO refuses the shift without a blip, which is carried as a simulator override rather than as the real car.
